scope: Independent manual review of only v3 UI cases05/06 against the original frozen checks, actual answers, saved read evidence, actions and drafts. No paid/model/API calls, source edits or SDK integration execution.

cases.manual_assessment: requested checks pass with minor teaching limitations

checks.name: Dataset-to-agent-to-score wiring
checks.evidence: Defines task list as the dataset, describes request/success_criteria, and shows inputs=task -> run_agent_turn(task[user_request]) -> pred.output -> judge_task_completion(task, transcript) -> pred.log_score. This is a valid documented imperative evaluation route.

checks.name: Documented execution path
checks.evidence: EvaluationLogger/log_prediction/start_conversation/log_score/log_summary match agent-evals section4. Setup and manual versus automatic instrumentation are explained from section3. Application helper functions are identified as placeholders and linked to complete notebook definitions. No implementation run is claimed.

checks.name: LLM judge explanation
checks.evidence: Explains plain-function judge reading trajectory against success criteria and returning passed/reason fields. Does not invent a built-in judge or claim perfect grading. The shorthand {passed,reason} describes dict fields as in the source prose, not an executed Python set.

cases.manual_assessment: requested checks pass with minor teaching limitations
cases.usefulness: Useful observed offline scoring example and clearly separated Weave logging route; includes results navigation.

checks.name: Actual offline execution
checks.evidence: One recorded run_python exits0 and prints True, False, True with accuracy0.6666666666666666. The answer correctly reports 2/3 and the case-sensitive Paris/paris mismatch. Source code contains built-ins only and no service calls.

checks.name: Separate execution from integration
checks.evidence: Explicitly says the plain-Python run only shows scoring logic and the EvaluationLogger integration was not run. The adapted example logs one actual sample output with a boolean score using documented log_example, initialization and summary calls.

checks.name: Context and no-service request
checks.evidence: Same conversation ID, prior evaluation exchange and retained sources. Refers to the prior LLM-judge answer, distinguishes simple output checks from trajectory evaluation, and only the offline Python snippet was executed.

issues: The Call-tab claim is only partly supported. S2 describes a `passed` column showing the LLM judge's verdict, where the score was a {"passed","reason"} dict logged through log_score. The answer's log_example snippet logs a bare boolean under the key "exact_match". The sources don't show that the Call tab displays a verdict for that shape. Qualify the claim, or log a dict like the tutorial does.
The answer says "Exact match works for checking final answers." That is the author's recommendation, not a sourced fact. Frame it as a recommendation.
The log_example snippet omits weave.init(...), which the cited S5 example includes. The snippet won't log to a project as written. Add the init call or say it is omitted.
Revise partial or unsupported material claims.
Minor: the log_example snippet is untested and uses the documented signature (inputs, output, scores); this is disclosed in the caveats.
The note that no documentation was seen on bare boolean score display is an honest limit, not a product claim.

findings.observation: Final paragraph still disclaims not reading weave.Dataset publication, multi-turn scoring and comparison sections, although the user asked a generic dataset/judge workflow and the documented task-list route answers it.
findings.effect: Adds uncertainty to an otherwise clear answer. This draft passed first time; unlike v2, the caveat was generated by the planner and was not introduced by a repair. No final false abstention.
findings.fairness: Do not require a weave.Dataset object, weave.Evaluation class, predict method or exhaustive related features when the imperative route is valid.

findings.observation: The answer explains initialization and instrumentation more clearly than the prior answer but its displayed loop still relies on imports, tasks and application helpers rather than being a standalone program. Those helpers are expressly identified.
findings.effect: Useful integration outline; no SDK execution claim. The question did not demand a complete executable project.

findings.observation: The execution record contains the full task list and scoring loop, but the displayed first block shows only the scorer and output comments.
findings.effect: Observed output is accurate and actual execution is established. A beginner would learn more from the full small example; this is not failure of the requested run.

findings.observation: Draft1 was rejected principally for extending the tutorial Call-tab verdict description to a bare boolean score. Final answer keeps the general results path, scopes the passed-column detail to the tutorial and adds a boolean-display caveat; it also adds weave.init and labels exact-match use as a recommendation.
findings.cause_assessment: Sources support logging booleans and reviewing per-prediction scores, so general UI navigation is a reasonable synthesis. They do not establish an identical passed column for every score shape. A narrow distinction is fair; a blanket refusal to give the path would not be.
findings.effect: Useful navigation is retained, unlike the prior blanket claim of not reading UI docs. Initialization was a helpful setup addition. This does not justify requiring a verbatim end-to-end example for ordinary API composition.

findings.observation: The trajectory-versus-single-output caution cites S2. Although its selected section is section4, S2.page_context contains the introductory trajectory statement and matches Corpus; the citation is supported by supplied evidence.
findings.effect: Do not incorrectly report a citation error by inspecting section text while ignoring source-bound page context.

execution_evidence.limitation: No Weave SDK or remote API calls. This only checks local Python behavior.

summary.claim: Both requested interactions meet the original checks. No material unsupported API or false execution claim found; remaining limits concern teaching brevity and unnecessary qualification.
